name: Yoke Figurative
overview: The figurative use of the yoke in Scripture vividly illustrates God's sovereign power to break the burdens and oppressive bonds placed upon His people. Passages such as Leviticus 26:13 and Jeremiah 28:2 emphasize God's deliverance by breaking the yoke of bondage, whether from Egypt or Babylon, setting His people free to walk upright. Similarly, Isaiah 9:4 and 10:27 portray the removal of oppressive yokes as a result of God's anointing and intervention, symbolizing liberation from heavy burdens and enemies. Jeremiah 2:20 and 5:5 further highlight the people's failure to remain under God's righteous yoke, underscoring the tension between divine authority and human rebellion.
